ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, a regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ with side length 2 has its center coinciding with the origin $O$, and $AB$ is parallel to the x-axis, intersecting the y-axis at point $P$. If $\triangle OAP$ is rotated clockwise around point $O$, rotating $90^\circ$ each time, what are the coordinates of point $A$ after the 2022nd rotation?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given a regular hexagon ABCDEF with side length 2, and its center coincides with the origin O,\\
\[ \because OA=AB=2, \angle BAO=60^\circ, \]
\[ \because AB\parallel x \text{ axis}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle APO=90^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle AOP=30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore AP=1, OP=\sqrt{3}, \]
\[ \therefore A(1,\sqrt{3}), \]
\[ \because \text{rotating } \triangle OAP \text { clockwise around point O by } 90^\circ\text{ each time, it is known that point A}_2 \text{ coincides with } D, \]
\[ \text{Since } 360^\circ \div 90^\circ=4, \]
\[ \text{indicating each cycle consists of 4 rotations,} \]
\[ \therefore 2022 \div 4=505\ldots 2, \]
\[ \therefore \text{point A}_{2022} \text{ coincides with point A}_2, \]
\[ \because \text{point A}_2 \text{ is symmetric to point A concerning the origin } O, \]
\[ \therefore A_2(-1,-\sqrt{3}), \]
\[ \therefore \text{after the 2022nd rotation, the coordinates of point A are} \boxed{(-1,-\sqrt{3})}\].

method.method_draft: Use the shaded right triangle OAP to locate A first, then use rotation periodicity. From the image, note that AB is the top horizontal side, P is where this side crosses the y-axis, OP is vertical, and A is to the right of the y-axis above the x-axis. From the text, use that the regular hexagon has side length 2 and center O, so OA equals the side length, 2. Since AB is parallel to the x-axis and OP lies on the y-axis, angle APO is 90 degrees. In a regular hexagon, triangle OAB is equilateral, so angle OAB is 60 degrees; therefore triangle OAP is a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse OA=2. Hence AP=1 and OP=sqrt(3), giving A=(1,sqrt(3)). Each clockwise 90-degree rotation repeats every 4 rotations; 2022 mod 4 = 2, so the final position is the result of two 90-degree rotations, i.e. a 180-degree rotation about O. Apply origin symmetry to A to get (-1,-sqrt(3)).

再推理：正六边形边长为 2，中心到顶点的距离等于边长，所以 OA=2。因为 AB 平行于 x 轴，OP 在 y 轴上，所以 ∠APO=90°。又因为正六边形中三角形 OAB 为等边三角形，所以 ∠OAB=60°，因此三角形 OAP 是 30°-60°-90°直角三角形，且斜边 OA=2。于是 AP=1，OP=√3。结合图中 A 在第一象限，可得 A=(1,√3)。

每次绕 O 顺时针旋转 90°，4 次为一个周期。2022÷4=505 余 2，所以第 2022 次旋转后的位置等同于旋转 2 次，即绕原点旋转 180°。点 (1,√3) 关于原点对称后为 (-1,-√3)。

method.method_draft: Use polar coordinates for the regular hexagon vertices, then reduce the net rotation angle. From the image, the hexagon is oriented with C and F on the x-axis and A as the upper-right vertex, so the ray OA makes a 60-degree angle with the positive x-axis. From the text, the side length is 2 and O is the center; in a regular hexagon the distance from the center to any vertex is also 2. Therefore A has polar coordinates (2, 60 degrees), so A=(2 cos 60 degrees, 2 sin 60 degrees)=(1,sqrt(3)). The 2022 clockwise rotations by 90 degrees give a net angle change of -2022*90 degrees. raw_record.original_question: In the Cartesian coordinate system, a regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ with side length 2 has its center at the origin $O$. Segment $AB$ is parallel to the x-axis and intersects the y-axis at point $P$. If $\triangle OAP$ is rotated clockwise about point $O$ by $90^\circ$ each time, what are the coordinates of point $A$ after the 2022nd rotation?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given a regular hexagon ABCDEF with side length 2, and its center coincides with the origin O,\\
\[ \because OA=AB=2, \angle BAO=60^\circ, \]
\[ \because AB\parallel x \text{ axis}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle APO=90^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle AOP=30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore AP=1, OP=\sqrt{3}, \]
\[ \therefore A(1,\sqrt{3}), \]
\[ \because \text{rotating } \triangle OAP \text { clockwise around point O by } 90^\circ\text{ each time, it is known that point A}_2 \text{ coincides with } D, \]
\[ \text{Since } 360^\circ \div 90^\circ=4, \]
\[ \text{indicating each cycle consists of 4 rotations,} \]
\[ \therefore 2022 \div 4=505\ldots 2, \]
\[ \therefore \text{point A}_{2022} \text{ coincides with point A}_2, \]
\[ \because \text{point A}_2 \text{ is symmetric to point A concerning the origin } O, \]
\[ \therefore A_2(-1,-\sqrt{3}), \]
\[ \therefore \text{after the 2022nd rotation, the coordinates of point A are} \boxed{(-1,-\sqrt{3})}\]
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is a regular hexagon ABCDEF with O as the center, O is at the coordinate origin, the x-axis is horizontal, and the y-axis is vertical. Side AB is located above and is horizontal, and intersects the y-axis at P. The shaded part is triangle OAP, where OP is on the y-axis, AP is on the horizontal side AB, and A is located to the right of the y-axis and above the x-axis.

Then reason: The side length of the regular hexagon is 2, and the distance from the center to a vertex equals the side length, so OA=2. Because AB is parallel to the x-axis and OP is on the y-axis, ∠APO=90°. Also because triangle OAB in the regular hexagon is an equilateral triangle, ∠OAB=60°, therefore triangle OAP is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, and the hypotenuse OA=2. Thus AP=1, OP=√3. Combining with the fact that A in the figure is in the first quadrant, A=(1,√3) can be obtained.

Each time it rotates clockwise around O by 90°, 4 times is one period. 2022÷4=505 remainder 2, so the position after the 2022nd rotation is equivalent to rotating 2 times, that is, rotating 180° around the origin. Point (1,√3) after being symmetric about the origin is (-1,-√3).
